question.text: The following concentrations were observed at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> for the formation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. At equilibrium : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo>,</mo><mfenced close="]" open="["><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math>. Equilibrium constant for the reaction is ______.

solution.text:
The equilibrium constant of concentration (denoted by Kc) of a chemical reaction at equilibrium can be defined as the ratio of the concentration of products to the concentration of the reactants, each raised to their respective stoichiometric coefficients.

The equilibrium reaction is 

N2g+3H2g⇋2NH3g

Kc=NH32H23N2

  =32×10-223×10-23×2×10-2

   =32×10-422×33×10-6×2×10-2

 =14×2×3×104=1000024=416.6≈417
